surfaces.label: G1 L2 front (cemented doublet L2-L3 front)
G1 L3 rear / variable air gap to G2F
G2F L4 front (cemented doublet L4-L5 front)

asph.convention: patent lists K = 195.0000 with an A3 term (-0.20873E-06) as well; A3 is an odd-order sag term not representable by this engine's even-order polynomial, so it is recorded here in notes rather than dropped silently. K is the conic constant added directly to the standard sag formula (not a kappa=K+1 convention) per the patent's own equation.

surfaces.label: G2R L7 front (cemented doublet L7-L8 front, aspheric)
G2R L9 front (cemented doublet L9-L10 front)
G2R L10 rear / last surface, t = Bf

gaps.note: d5 in the patent's own numbering (surface 5, 1-based); the patent lists an intermediate 'Close Range 1' state too (d5=6.32841 at object distance 1062.6389 mm) which is not stored here, only infinity and the nearest close range; object distance is the patent's own d0 column, reference point (front surface vs. subject) not stated in the excerpted text

focus.minFocusSource: assumed - typical minimum focus for a fast 35 mm f/1.4-class full-frame prime, order-of-magnitude comparison only, NOT this patent example. Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 35mm f/1.4G spec page (https://www.nikonusa.com/p/af-s-nikkor-35mm-f14g/2198/overview, fetched 9/28/2026) states minimum focus '0.98 ft.' = 0.30 m and '9' diaphragm blades. This patent example's filing (priority 9/28/2007, granted 2/16/2010) is close in time to that lens's 2/2010 announcement, which is a real coincidence worth noting, but no public source confirms this exact 17-surface/10-element prescription is that product's actual design, so the tie is NOT recorded as representativeOf

iris.source: assumed - typical rounded-blade count for a fast 35 mm-class prime of this era; not tied to this specific patent example

notes: Source is Nikon US 7,663,816 B2 'Wide-angle lens and imaging apparatus' (priority JP 2007-254903, filed 9/28/2007; US application filed 8/5/2008; granted 2/16/2010). Text read directly from the Google Patents description section (English original, not a translation).

The patent's own nominal marketed class for this design family is described in the spec as a 'wide-angle lens' around f=36 mm at Fno 1.45; focalLength here is recorded as 35 (the requested class) while stated.f keeps the patent's own raw value 36.000, per the schema's distinction between marketed class and patent-stated f. Examples 2-4 in the same patent are f=35.863 mm (closer to nominal 35) but add a zero-thickness 'Flare Stopper' surface (r=infinity, d=0 between the front and middle groups) that Example 1 does not have; Example 1 was used for simplicity and because it was the one fully self-checked.

Surface 12 (first surface of the rear aspheric cemented doublet) has a patent-listed A3 term (-0.20873E-06) in addition to K, A4, A6, A8, A10, A12. This engine's Asphere type only supports even orders (A4, A6, ...); the A3 term is recorded here in the surface's asph.convention note rather than silently dropped, and the self-check (which is paraxial/first-order only) is unaffected since neither A3 nor any other aspheric term enters a paraxial trace.

K=195.0000 on surface 12: the patent's own text states this uses the sag equation x = c*h^2/(1+sqrt(1-(1+K)*c^2*h^2)) + A4 h^4 + ... i.e. the SAME convention as lens-types.ts (K=0 is a sphere), not a kappa=K+1 convention. Recorded as k:195.0 directly.
Surfaces 3-4, 6-7, 12-13 and 15-16 are cemented doublets (shared vertex, second glass on the same table row) per patent convention; those interfaces marked coated:false.

The patent gives THREE focus states (Infinity, Close Range 1, Close Range 2); only Infinity and Close Range 2 (the nearest) are stored in focus.gaps per the LensDesign schema's two-state VariableGap; Close Range 1 (object distance 1062.6389 mm, d5=6.32841, d8=7.55812) is noted here in prose instead: it sits between the two stored states and is available in the patent if the engine ever wants a third state.

No effective/clear-diameter table anywhere in the patent text; all surfaces use sdSource 'estimated-from-marginal-ray' via the two-ray paraxial method in .local/lens-wide/raytrace.py, scaled to the patent's own stated Fno=1.45 and half field 31.53 deg.
medium is 'glass' everywhere (no named glass catalog in the patent, only nd/vd).

No public source ties this patent example to a specific shipped Nikon product; representativeOf is intentionally omitted (see minFocusSource note for the circumstantial timing only, which is not a citation of identity).
